editorial.meta_description: The CCDS Certified Cardiac Device Specialist exam evaluates professional knowledge of cardiac rhythm management, device technology, and patient follow-up.
editorial.overview: The CCDS Certified Cardiac Device Specialist exam, administered by the IBHRE (International Board of Heart Rhythm Examiners), evaluates knowledge of cardiac rhythm management. It covers ten distinct domains, including electrophysiology, engineering concepts, device algorithms, and patient follow-up management. This 200-question exam assesses the clinical and technical skills required for professionals working with cardiac implantable electronic devices in a healthcare setting.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification is intended for healthcare professionals involved in the management of cardiac implantable electronic devices. Candidates should possess experience in clinical assessment, perioperative practice, and device follow-up management to address the technical and patient-care requirements of this field.
skills_summary: Engineering and electrical concepts for devices
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the ten domains, focusing on patient and device follow-up management, which accounts for 20% of the score. Study device algorithms and functions, as they represent 14% of the content. Use the official IBHRE exam guide to understand the scope of the 200 questions. Practice interpreting electrocardiograms and fluoroscopy images to prepare for the clinical assessment and radiology sections of the exam.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the anatomy and physiology of the heart and conduction system, along with the mechanisms of various dysrhythmias that require clinical intervention and management by cardiac device professionals.

This section focuses on the engineering and electrical concepts necessary for understanding pulse generators, leads, and defibrillation, ensuring that candidates can apply these technical principles to cardiac device performance and maintenance.

This domain covers device technology, including sensing, stimulation, and timing cycles for various device types, providing the technical foundation required to evaluate how different cardiac devices function within the human cardiovascular system.

This domain addresses device functions and algorithms for bradycardia, tachycardia, and heart failure management, ensuring that specialists can effectively program and troubleshoot devices to meet the specific needs of their patients.

This section covers the interpretation of electrocardiograms and wearable monitor data to identify rhythms and malfunctions, allowing professionals to accurately assess device performance and detect potential issues during routine patient follow-up visits.

This domain focuses on clinical assessment, device indications, and the impact of pharmacology on device therapy, helping candidates understand how patient history and medication regimens influence the selection and management of cardiac devices.

This section covers perioperative and intraoperative practices, including surgical techniques, infection prevention, and radiation safety, ensuring that specialists can support safe and effective device implantation procedures within a sterile clinical operating environment.

This domain addresses safety practices regarding radiation, EMI, MRI compatibility, and device advisories, providing the knowledge necessary to protect patients from environmental hazards and ensure the long-term integrity of their implanted cardiac devices.

This section focuses on the interpretation of radiological images, including X-rays, fluoroscopy, CT scans, and ultrasound, which are tools for verifying lead placement and identifying potential complications after a cardiac device implantation.

This domain covers patient and device follow-up management, including interrogation, programming, and troubleshooting, which represents the most significant portion of the exam and is vital for ongoing patient care and device optimization.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: The exam consists of 200 questions to be completed in 240 minutes. Ensure you are familiar with the content outline and the specific domains. Manage your time effectively across the ten domains to address all questions within the allotted duration to maximize your performance.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The CCDS Certified Cardiac Device Specialist exam is an assessment that consists of 200 questions, which are designed to test your clinical and technical knowledge of cardiac rhythm management and implantable device technology.

Candidates are provided with a total duration of 240 minutes to complete the entire exam. It is recommended that you manage your time carefully across all ten domains to ensure you have sufficient time to answer every question.

The CCDS Certified Cardiac Device Specialist exam is officially certified and administered by the IBHRE (International Board of Heart Rhythm Examiners), which sets the standards for professionals working in the field of cardiac rhythm management and device therapy.

faq.question_title: Where can I find the current certification path?
faq.answer_text: For detailed information regarding the current certification path and any updates to the exam requirements, please check with IBHRE (International Board of Heart Rhythm Examiners) directly through their official website to ensure you have the most accurate and up-to-date guidance.

methodology.summary: This page was built by synthesizing the official IBHRE exam content outline and candidate handbook to provide a structured, accurate, and overview of the CCDS certification requirements for all prospective candidates.
